language: python
hook: "Programmers read far more code than they write. The first skill is finding the part that does the job you want to change."
app:
  command: "node \"$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs\" \"$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground\" 8123"

This program is longer than any you have met, but it uses only things you know. The skill now is **reading**: finding which lines do which job.

## Predict

```step
stage: predict
code: garden.py#garden
check:
  type: predict
  q: "stem is 50. How tall is the third stem (when i is 2)?"
  kind: number
  actual: "70. The stem is stem + i * 10, which is 50 + 2 * 10 = 70. Each stem is 10 taller than the one before."
```

Read the code, one comment at a time. How tall is the third stem?

## Run

```step
stage: run
code: garden.py#garden
try: { starter: "garden.py#garden", height: 440 }
check: { type: reflect, text: "I can point to the lines that draw a stem, the lines that draw a flower head, and the line that makes the flowers repeat." }
```

Run it and compare it with your prediction. Which part is the turtle running right now?

## Investigate

```step
stage: investigate
code: garden.py#garden
insight: "A longer program is made of parts that each do one job. Find the part, see what it depends on, and you can change it without breaking the rest."
tasks:
  - diagram:
      ref: diagrams.mmd#parts
      alt: "A flowchart of one pass of the loop, once for each colour. First a decision: is i even? Yes gives a green stem, no a dark green stem. Then draw the stem, taller each time. Then fill the flower head and grow the next head by 4. Then go back down and along 70, and start the next flower."
      caption: "One pass of the garden loop"
      role: explain
    check:
      type: match
      q: "Match each part of the program with its job."
      pairs:
        - ["if i % 2 == 0: ... else: ...", "alternates the stem between two greens"]
        - ["forward(stem + i * 10)", "makes each stem taller than the last"]
        - ["head = head + 4", "makes each flower head bigger than the last"]
        - ["colours[i]", "picks the flower's colour by its place"]
      explain: "Each line has one job. The if / else is a decision, i * 10 uses the counter, head + 4 is an update, and colours[i] is a list item picked by its place."
  - check:
      type: bug
      code: garden.py#bug
      text: "The flower heads should grow, but all four are the same size. Click the line that stops them growing."
      answer: 16
      fault: logic
      misconception: update-outside-loop
      explain: "head = 10 is inside the loop, so it is reset to 10 at the start of every pass, and the update never gets a chance to add up. Set it once before the loop."
```

### Find the parts

Match each part with its job.

### Spot the bug

The update is there, but something undoes it.

## Modify

```step
stage: modify
insight: "Change one part at a time and run after each change; the rest of the program should keep working."
try: { starter: "garden.py#modify", height: 440 }
tasks:
  - hint:
      - "Which line holds the list of colours? Add to it."
      - "Six flowers are wider than four. Move the start further left with goto."
    check: { type: code, text: "Add two more flowers that fit on the screen.", rules: { contains: ["colours = ["], uses: [goto] } }
  - hint:
      - "Which part of the program makes the stems different heights?"
      - "Where it says stem + i * 10, take away the part that uses i."
    check: { type: reflect, text: "I changed only the stem lines, and every stem is the same height." }
```

### Add flowers

Add two more colours. Everything else should keep working.

### Same height

Find the part that makes the stems different, and change only that.

You've found the parts by their jobs. Over the next few lessons you'll give those parts names, so you can use them again and again.

```code diagrams.mmd#parts
flowchart TD
  A[For each colour in the list] --> B{"Is i even?"}
  B -- yes --> C[Green stem]
  B -- no --> D[Dark green stem]
  C --> E[Draw stem, taller each time]
  D --> E
  E --> F[Fill head, then grow it]
  F -- back down and along --> A
  class B new
```

```teacher
summary: Students read a longer program that combines the counter, a list, an
  update and a decision, find the lines that do each job, and change one part
  without breaking the rest.
time: 35
timing: Predict and Run 10 min · Investigate 12 min · Modify 13 min
goals:
  - I can find the lines that do one job in a longer program.
  - I can say what a part depends on before I change it.
  - I can change one part and keep the rest working.
before: >
  Run the garden, then do the Modify tasks yourself. The program is a loop with
  a long body: that length is what the next lesson fixes.
running:
  - "Predict: read the code with the class, one comment at a time. The stem line
    uses the counter; ask what i is on the third pass."
  - "Run: students run it and watch which part the turtle is drawing. Ask: which
    lines draw a stem? Which draw a flower head?"
  - "Investigate: the match task names each part's job. The bug is a reset: a
    value set inside the loop is set again every pass."
  - "Modify: students change one part at a time. If the extra flowers run off
    the screen, ask which line moves the start."
stuck:
  - see: The extra flowers run off the screen.
    ask: Where does the first flower start, and how far apart are the flowers?
    fix: Move the start further left with goto, for example goto(-200, -80).
  - see: Changing one thing breaks another.
    ask: Which other lines use the name you changed?
    fix: Find every line that uses it before you change it. A name is used wherever
      it appears.
stretch: Make every other flower head a different shape by adding a decision to
  the flower-head lines.
support: Colour or underline the lines for each job on paper before changing anything.
leads: Next lesson names a group of lines (a function). The garden's long loop
  body is the first thing to name.
exit:
  q: In the garden, which part would you change to make every flower head the same
    size?
  a: The update head = head + 4. Remove it, or set head once and never add to it.
explain: >
  A longer program is made of parts that each do one job: a decision, a
  calculation with the counter, an update, a list item picked by its place. Read
  for the **job** first, not every symbol. Then change only the part that does
  the job you want to change.
solutions:
  step-4#t1: garden.py#sol-colours
  step-4#t2: garden.py#sol-same
struggle: Knowing which lines to change. Ask what job the new feature is, then
  which lines do that job.
class:
  activities:
    - at: start
      kind: info
      title: By the end of this lesson
      do: >
        Here is the finished program running. By the end of the lesson you will
        write one like it.
      notes: Run the finished example on the projector before anything else.
    - at: investigate
      title: Highlight the jobs
      minutes: 5
      do: >
        Pairs colour the garden lines on paper: stem, head, spacing, decision.
        Compare with the next pair.
      notes: Make the idea physical before it goes back to the screen.
```
files.garden.py:
# region: garden
from turtle import *

speed(0)
colours = ["red", "orange", "pink", "purple"]
stem = 50
head = 10

penup()
goto(-150, -80)
pendown()

for i in range(len(colours)):
    # stem
    if i % 2 == 0:
        pencolor("green")
    else:
        pencolor("darkgreen")
    pensize(3)
    left(90)
    forward(stem + i * 10)

    # flower head
    fillcolor(colours[i])
    begin_fill()
    circle(head)
    end_fill()
    head = head + 4

    # back down, then along to the next flower
    penup()
    backward(stem + i * 10)
    right(90)
    forward(70)
    pendown()
# endregion
